name: PT Jaya Real Property, Tbk.

frontmatter.title: Jaya Real Property — a fortress balance sheet at a premium to asset value
frontmatter.summary: Jaya Real Property's third-quarter filing shows nine-month revenue and profit up double digits on last year, marketing sales ahead of the run-rate, and the net-cash balance sheet intact. The operating story is unchanged; the valuation is not. Marking the land to a sourced fraction of its published market range and applying the sector's standing RNAV discount band moves us to REDUCE.
thesis: Quality, cash-generative developer: a mature township, net cash and a recurring-income base, with return on equity around 12.7%.

Presales are growing but not inflecting: marketing sales of IDR1,950bn in the first nine months were ahead of last year's IDR1,770bn but are already reflected in a share price at 10.6x forward earnings and 1.3x book.

The asset case is real but not a floor at today's price: valuing the land at a sourced fraction of the Bintaro market range and applying the sector discount band gives an RNAV value of Rp1,011, below the Rp1,175 quote.
Recurring income covers the cost base and there is no debt, so the downside is valuation, not solvency; the bear case is Rp841 against a base of Rp1,064.
We move to REDUCE with a twelve-month target of Rp970, a return of -14.6%; the land mark and the band, not a call on the township, move the value.
What would change it: a named catalyst that narrows the discount — a rate-cut cycle, a land or associate monetisation, or a disclosed appraisal confirming a higher wholesale land value.

catalysts.event: FY2026 marketing sales announcement (company publishes the annual figure in late January)
FY2026 audited results and dividend declaration
Annual general meeting and final dividend approval

blocks.text: This is the results update for the third quarter of 2026. The nine-month filing shows revenue of IDR2,540bn, gross profit of IDR1,389bn and net profit attributable to the parent of IDR1,009bn, each ahead of the same period last year, with basic earnings per share of Rp79 [S5]. Marketing sales reached IDR1,950bn in the first nine months against IDR1,770bn a year earlier, led by Bintaro Jaya at IDR1,150bn [S9]. The operating story is intact and the balance sheet is still net cash. The operating result does not change the valuation arithmetic: we move from HOLD to REDUCE and cut the twelve-month target to Rp970 from one thousand and fifty-eight rupiah, because at Rp1,175 the shares trade above our market-marked RNAV even after the 40.0% discount — a price that assumes the land is worth far more than the sourced mark we credit.

Jaya Real Property is the developer of Bintaro Jaya, a mature planned township in South Tangerang, together with Graha Raya, Serpong Jaya and Puri Jaya, and it owns the retail, hotel, water-park and estate-management businesses inside those estates [S7]. It is conservatively financed: debt is immaterial, cash and deposits exceed it, and the company has funded land acquisition and investment property from operating cash flow for years [S5]. Revenue and net profit have compounded at a steady rate through a difficult property cycle, and the dividend has risen every year since the pandemic [S3][S7].

The problem is the price, and this revision changes our answer on it. At Rp1,175 the shares are worth IDR15,016.8bn, or 10.6x our FY2026 earnings and 1.3x our FY2026 book value [S0]. That is the top of the company's own four-year multiple range and a clear premium to the sector. Our primary method is RNAV, built on three blocks on their own bases: land for development at market with a stated haircut, development inventory at cost net of customer advances, investment property capitalised at a market yield, and the associate stakes at book [S5][S7][S10]. The land is no longer taken at audited cost: the published Bintaro Jaya land range is 7m rupiah per square metre at its low end [S10], and we credit only a small fraction of it, a stated wholesale and infrastructure haircut, which still leaves the land block well above carrying cost. On that market-based RNAV we apply the floor of the method card's forty-to-seventy per cent band, 40.0%, giving an RNAV value of Rp1,011. The discount is not a haircut on conservatism twice: it is the sector's standing discount to a NAV that now carries a market land value, and it is the same construction the covered peers use on cost-based land. Our blended value is Rp970, a return of -14.6%, and the rating moves to REDUCE.

The variant view is therefore about the asset mark, not the township's quality, which we accept. The market pays a premium to our discounted market-marked RNAV and a premium multiple for a business whose growth is mature, whose public float is 15.2% of the register and whose shares trade IDR719.3m a day [S6][S0]. The company cannot create the catalyst that would justify the premium: the macro deck holds the policy rate flat through the forecast, so mortgage affordability does not improve on our numbers, and there is no dated re-rating event. The free-float overhang in the previous draft is withdrawn: the company register shows the public holding above the minimum the exchange now requires, so there is no forced placement inside the horizon [S6][S11]. Recurring income and net cash protect the downside — the bear case is Rp841, not a solvency story — but they do not make the equity cheap.

JRPT develops and sells land lots, houses, shophouses and condominiums, and it owns and operates the commercial and leisure assets that give the township its value. The development segment generated IDR2,292bn of revenue in FY2025 and the recurring segment IDR1,030bn, so roughly a third of the top line is rental, estate management, hotel, oceanarium, service charge, ice rink, sports club, water park and driving range [S7]. The mix matters: development earnings are lumpy and handover-driven, while the recurring businesses generate cash every month and, on our numbers, cover the cost base several times over.

The land bank is the franchise. The company states that it still holds 1,743 hectares within its existing townships, with Bintaro Jaya the largest component and the balance in Graha Raya, Serpong Jaya, Puri Jaya and the Pasar Kemis and Rajeg land [S4]. Bintaro Jaya is a mature estate with tens of thousands of households, international schools, a commuter-train stop, toll-road access and its own malls and hospital; the company describes its strategy as monetising land selectively to fund operations, replenish the bank and invest in facilities that raise the value of what remains [S4]. That is a credible, patient township model rather than a high-turnover housing builder.

The model has three engines. First, land and building sales: FY2025 revenue was led by land lots, then building units, then condominiums, with land alone contributing the largest single line [S7]. Second, recurring income: Bintaro Jaya Xchange and Bintaro Plaza malls, the Bintaro Trade Center, hotels, the Aviary Park oceanarium and water parks, estate management and water services [S6][S7]. Third, strategic investments: a direct stake in the Jakarta Tollroad Development concession, a hospital joint venture with Pondok Indah, and water and estate-services associates, carried at book within a balance sheet that remains unlevered [S7].

The company is controlled by PT Pembangunan Jaya, which holds 67.7% of the shares; a BNP Paribas Singapore nominee holds a further 16.5% and the public below the five per cent line holds 15.2% [S6]. The public float therefore sits above the minimum the exchange is moving to under Rule I-A, not below it as the previous draft claimed from the data pack, and there is no placement or forced-sale event in the forecast [S6][S11]. The register is dated 31 December 2025 and the company also held a small treasury position at that date [S6]. It employs 477 people directly [S0]. The group's origins are in the Pembangunan Jaya foundation and the Ancol development company, and the controlling shareholder has been stable for decades [S7].

Strategically, management is doing the sensible things: launching mid-market landed products in Bintaro and Puri Jaya, completing the Creativo tower at Bintaro Plaza Residences, maintaining tenant mix in the malls and investing in healthcare and toll-road assets that throw off recurring income [S7]. None of this is a step-change. The company's own revenue target for FY2025 was beaten by a modest margin, and its growth has come from volume and price in an existing township rather than from new geography [S7].

Indonesian residential demand is a mortgage product. Purchase decisions key off affordability — the policy rate, bank mortgage rates and the availability of down-payment support — with a lag of several quarters, and developers' reported revenue lags marketing sales by one to two years because revenue is recognised on handover [S7]. That makes presales the only clean read on current demand, and it makes the rate path the single most important external variable for the sector. The house macro deck has the policy rate at 5.8% in FY2027, CPI at 3.3%, real GDP growth at 5.3% and the rupiah at 18,350 to the dollar; that is a stable, not an easing, backdrop for mortgages and it comes from the house deck, not from the annual report.

Indonesian developers typically sell land and houses off-plan, collect customer advances, and recognise revenue when the unit is handed over. Listed developers therefore report marketing sales (presales) monthly or quarterly as their key operating metric, and their shares have historically traded at persistent discounts to appraised net asset value because of governance concerns, land-title risk and the cyclicality of the cycle. Greater Jakarta's oversupply in high-rise condominiums has been a feature of the last cycle, while landed housing in established townships with schools and transport has held up better.

JRPT's position is unusual. It is not a volume housebuilder competing on new launches across the city; it is the owner-manager of a township that has been developing for decades, with a land bank that was assembled decades ago at very low cost [S4][S7]. That gives it a structural margin advantage — development gross margin has held around 55.4% at the group level and the segment margin is higher — and it gives it control over the quality of the estate. Bintaro Jaya's connectivity improved with the toll roads and the commuter line, and the company continues to develop transit-oriented schemes around the Bintaro Xchange masterplan [S4]. Its main competition is other township and landed developers in the western and southern Greater Jakarta corridor, not the CBD high-rise builders.

The competitive moat is real but bounded. Real is the land: within Bintaro there is no substitute for a Bintaro address, and the company owns the commercial centres that anchor it. Bounded is the growth: the township is mature, new launches are incremental, and the company's own marketing-sales record shows single-digit-to-low-double-digit growth over a full cycle rather than a compounding runway [S6]. Marketing sales went from IDR2,277bn in FY2024 to IDR2,467bn in FY2025 and reached IDR1,950bn in the first nine months of FY2026, up double digits year on year, with Bintaro Jaya contributing the majority [S8][S9]. That is a good outcome in a soft market, but it is the performance of a mature asset, not of a growth company.

Five forces, briefly. Supplier power is moderate: land in the corridor is scarce but the company already owns most of what it needs, and contractors are plentiful. Buyer power is rising: buyers have many Greater Jakarta alternatives and are rate-sensitive. New entrants are constrained by land availability and permits in established corridors, which favours incumbents. Substitutes are resale homes and rental, both active. Rivalry is high in high-rise and moderate in landed township product. The net effect is a business that defends margin through location rather than pricing power [S7].

Regulation and external influences cut both ways. Property is a policy-sensitive sector: land acquisition, permits, the tax treatment of land and building sales, and mortgage rules all move the economics. JRPT's final tax on land and building sales is already embedded in its reported profitability [S5]. The rupiah matters less than for dollar-indebted peers because the company has no material foreign-currency debt [S5]. The main macro transmission is through buyer affordability. Because the deck holds the policy rate at spot with inflation near target, real affordability is broadly unchanged rather than deteriorating, so we treat the flat path as neutral and put the rate downside in the bear case rather than the base [S5].

Revenue grew from IDR2,259bn in FY2022 to IDR3,275bn in FY2025, a compound rate in the high single digits, with FY2025 growth of 11.1% [S0][S7]. The growth was broad: land sales rose, building units were steady, condominium revenue more than doubled on handovers, and recurring revenue grew double digits as the oceanarium and hotel recovered [S7]. Gross margin was 55.4%, EBITDA margin 45.1% and net margin 39.8%, all consistent with a developer selling land carried at historic cost [S7].

The third-quarter filing is the first hard read on our FY2026 build. Revenue of IDR2,540bn in the first nine months compares with our FY2026 estimate of IDR3,627bn; gross profit was IDR1,389bn on operating expenses of IDR357bn, leaving operating profit of IDR1,044bn and an operating margin close to the FY2025 outcome [S5]. Financial income of IDR53bn is the net-cash balance sheet doing the work, and the final-tax charge held at about the same share of revenue as last year [S5]. Net profit attributable to the parent of IDR1,009bn and EPS of Rp79 compare with our FY2026 estimates of IDR1,427bn and Rp111; the implied fourth quarter grows revenue at a single-digit rate against a double-digit nine months, which is the seasonal pattern we built, and we leave the forecast unchanged [S5][S9]. One detail is worth flagging for earnings quality: customer advances of IDR2,876bn at 30 September 2026 sit marginally below the year-end 2025 balance in the same filing, so presales growth was absorbed into handovers rather than building the liability further. That is a timing effect on the liability side, not a demand signal, and the presales book itself grew [S5][S9].

We restate the depreciation line from the financial statements. The data pack carries depreciation of a few billion rupiah, which captures only the administrative charge; the audited accounts show depreciation of IDR118bn in FY2025 and IDR114bn in FY2024, almost all of it allocated to cost of revenues and direct expenses on the investment properties [S7]. We therefore restate the last two years and rebuild EBITDA. FY2025 EBITDA is IDR1,478bn on our numbers rather than the pack's lower figure, and the restatement leaves net profit unchanged because the charge was already inside cost of sales [S7].

Our forecast is a build, not a trend extrapolation. Marketing sales grow 8.0% in FY2026 and taper to 4.0% by FY2030, consistent with the first-nine-months run-rate and the company's mature township [S9]. Development revenue is a weighted blend of current and prior-year presales, calibrated so that FY2025 development revenue is reproduced within a few percentage points [S6][S7]. Recurring revenue grows 6.0% in FY2026, below the FY2025 reopening spike, and tapers thereafter [S7]. That gives revenue of IDR3,627bn in FY2026 and IDR3,886bn in FY2027, growth of 10.8% and 7.1%.

Margins are held at the last actual, not improved. Development gross margin is 57.0% and recurring gross margin 53.9%, both the FY2025 outcomes [S7]. SG&A is 14.1% of revenue, the FY2025 ratio [S7]. The result is EBITDA of IDR1,655bn and net profit to parent of IDR1,427bn in FY2026, with EPS of Rp111 and return on equity of 12.7%. The forecast does not assume a margin windfall from land-price inflation; if anything, the tax charge we apply is a little above the cash tax the company actually pays because the final tax sits above the line [S5].

Cash flow is the strongest part of the story. FY2025 operating cash flow comfortably covered capex, which is small because township infrastructure and land development sit in inventories rather than in fixed assets [S7]. The company ended FY2025 with cash of IDR1,373bn and net cash of IDR-1,369bn; the net cash position widens in our forecast to IDR-2,851bn and IDR-4,116bn as profits accumulate faster than dividends [S5][S7]. Net debt to EBITDA is -0.9 — negative, i.e. net cash — and there is no refinancing risk. The balance sheet also carries customer advances of IDR2,876bn, which fund construction and are the liability side of the presales book [S5].

Working capital is negative in the model because advances exceed receivables and inventory, which is normal for a developer selling off-plan [S0]. That flatters free cash flow in a growth year and reverses if presales slow; we flag it rather than celebrate it. Capex is forecast at 2.5% of revenue, between the two most recent years' cash-flow capex, and covers mall refurbishment and estate infrastructure [S7]. The dividend is Rp34 in FY2026, a payout of 30.7% of earnings, in line with the FY2025 distribution of Rp31 per share [S5].

Earnings quality screens. The accruals ratio is not a concern: net profit is backed by operating cash flow, and the gap between the two is explained by customer advances and depreciation inside cost of sales rather than by receivables [S7]. Receivables are a small share of revenue and related-party balances are disclosed separately [S7]. Capitalised borrowing costs are immaterial because there is almost no debt [S5]. The two flags that matter are structural rather than accounting: the public float on the company register is 15.2%, at or above the minimum the exchange now requires, and the controlling shareholder holds 67.7% of the shares with a 16.5% nominee block alongside it, so minority influence is limited [S6][S11]. We treat both as optics-class, disclosed and stable, not manipulation-class.

We value JRPT on RNAV, cross-checked with the company's own-history P/E and P/B, weighted 60% RNAV, 20% P/E and 20% P/B. RNAV is the right primary method for a land-owning township developer because the earnings stream is a function of when land is monetised, not of a steady-state margin; a DCF would put a spurious precision on handover timing. The multiple cross-checks keep us honest on what the market has been willing to pay for those earnings.

The RNAV has three asset blocks, and each now enters on its own stated basis rather than under one label. Land for development is marked to market with a stated haircut: the published Bintaro Jaya range is 7m rupiah per square metre at the low end for an individual serviced plot [S10], and we credit only a small fraction of that, reflecting the wholesale value of a whole land bank that includes roads, lakes, drainage, schools and utilities, the outlying estates outside Bintaro Jaya, and the age of the quote. That fraction still leaves the land block well above its carrying cost; the arithmetic is set out in the assumptions file. Development inventory enters at cost, net of customer advances, which is an identity rather than a haircut because the advances are funded cash already deducted in net debt [S5]. Investment property is capitalised on recurring gross profit at a market yield, which is the main write-up in the valuation, and the associate stakes enter at equity-method book [S5][S7]. The previous draft's claim that the whole RNAV was cost-based was wrong, and with it the argument that a band would discount the same conservatism twice: only the land was at cost, and the land is no longer.

Recurring assets are capitalised, not valued at book. We solve the cap rate back from a net operating income yield in the high single digits for Greater Jakarta suburban retail and mid-market hotels, after allocating the recurring share of SG&A; expressed on the gross profit the engine capitalises, the input is 12.4% [S5][S7]. On that gross-profit basis the covered peers run materially wider yields, so our rate is in the conservative half of the peer range rather than at its wide end, and the retail segment's 55.4% group-level margin at high occupancy supports it [S7]. The associate stakes — the toll-road concession, the hospital and the water businesses — are added at book [S7]. Book is the right basis for a forty-five-year toll-road concession at an early stage of its life, where equity book approximates invested capital and the apparent earnings multiple is high because the asset is still in ramp-up; shared profit of IDR36.9bn on a IDR347bn block is a low current yield, not an over-valuation, and a mark on current earnings would misprice a long-dated concession. The disclosure point is that a mark at a mid-teen earnings multiple would remove a material part of the block; we disclose that as the downside rather than adopt it, because no source supports it.

The cost of equity is 11.9%: a risk-free rate of 7.4%, an equity risk premium plus country risk, and a beta of 0.90, essentially the industry default because the company has no net debt [S0]. Because debt is immaterial, WACC is 11.9% and the capital structure is effectively all equity. The terminal growth of 4.0% is the house rate for rupiah cash flows and is used only in the DCF cross-check, which is not in the weight set.

The RNAV value after the target discount is Rp1,011 and the target discount is 40.0%, the floor of the method card's forty-to-seventy per cent band for IDX developers. The pre-discount RNAV is roughly one thousand six hundred and eighty-five rupiah a share, so at Rp1,175 the market is already applying a discount of about thirty per cent to it — roughly ten points tighter than our base. That gap is the call, and it is checkable: the discount axis moves the value by about one hundred and fifteen rupiah a share for every ten points, so the ten-point difference is worth about that much, and we take the wider discount because there is no dated catalyst to close it. We cannot show the name's own five-year RNAV-discount range because no archived source publishes a historical RNAV series for JRPT, so the floor is anchored to the method card and to the covered peers, which value land at carrying cost and still discount from the high twenties to the low seventies per cent, rather than to a house history we do not have. The previous draft set it to zero on the argument that the band haircuts only appraised land; that argument does not survive the peer files, which value land at carrying cost net of advances and still band it, with CTRA, PWON, MTLA, SMRA and CBDK running discounts from the high twenties to the low seventies per cent. We take the floor rather than the mid-band because JRPT is net cash, its recurring income covers the cost base several times, it has no foreign-currency debt and our land credit is deliberately only a small fraction of the published retail range. There is no dated catalyst for a tighter discount: the house macro deck holds the policy rate flat through FY2027, presales are compounding at trend rather than inflecting, and the company meets the free-float rule on its own register, so the supply event the previous draft leaned on does not exist [S6][S11]. The scenarios mirror the discount by fifteen points either side; no full-NAV convergence is assumed. The published target is the probability-weighted scenario value less the 10.0% liquidity discount. That discount is not an analyst overlay: it is the house limits table's explicit haircut for a name whose traded value is IDR719.3m a day, applied at the target line by the engine's construction and shown as its own line rather than buried in the cost of equity or in the peer selection.

The multiple cross-checks now sit close below the RNAV value rather than far below it: P/E gives Rp984, -2.7% below it, and P/B gives Rp893, -11.6% below it [S0]. Both are struck on the same as-of date as the RNAV: the P/E applies its own-history multiple to last-twelve-month net profit to the September quarter, not to the stale FY2025 figure the previous draft used, and P/B uses the September 2026 parent equity. The P/B number is the lower of the two, and the reason is visible in the table: book value captures retained earnings and net cash but neither the land mark nor the investment-property write-up, so it is a lagging proxy for an asset NAV and we do not let it set the value. We do not average the anchors away; we weight them and show the divergence, which is now small enough that the three methods agree in direction. The multiples are based on the company's own four-year history, a period in which the shares traded between a discount and a premium to book, and they capture the market's willingness to pay for net cash and recurring income. With the multiples at two-fifths of the weight, they pull the fundamental blend to Rp982, under the RNAV value of Rp1,011; the twelve-month construction then adds a year's cost of equity and deducts the next dividend, and the probability-weighted scenario value is Rp1,077 before the liquidity adjustment and Rp970 after it. Both sit below the Rp1,175 quote, and the gap is the call.

The sensitivity table shows what the call actually hinges on. A ten-percentage-point change in presales growth moves the twelve-month value by under two rupiah a share, because the anchors are the asset base and the own-history multiple, not a growth extrapolation. The discount axis moves the value by roughly one hundred and fifteen rupiah for every ten points, and its two ends span about two hundred and thirty. The grid is struck on the scenario value before the liquidity adjustment, so its central cell is Rp1,064 rather than the published Rp970; the target is the probability-weighted scenario value less the 10.0% liquidity discount. Presales is nearly irrelevant to the outcome and the discount is dominant. The land mark is the second lever: the bear and bull move it, and the assumptions file carries the fraction of the published range that we credit, so a reader can rebuild the value from the sourced benchmark.

What today's price implies is the mirror image. At Rp1,175 the shares sit above our RNAV value of Rp1,011, so the market is paying a premium to a NAV that already carries a market land value, an investment property at a mid-band yield and the associates at book [S5][S7]; measured against the pre-discount RNAV of roughly one thousand six hundred and eighty-five rupiah a share, the same price is a discount of about thirty per cent, ten points tighter than the base we publish. To close the gap on our construction, the market must be crediting a land value several times the fraction of the published Bintaro range we allow, or expecting the discount band to narrow to its tight end and stay there; neither has a dated trigger in the record. Equivalently, the price implies a return on equity divided by price-to-book below the cost of equity: the market is paying for the quality and getting a below-cost-of-equity return. The reverse DCF does not bracket a presales growth rate that justifies the price, which is consistent with the multiple cross-checks: earnings growth is not the lever, the asset mark and the band are. The honest reading is that the price is above the asset value on our most likely mark and above the own-history multiples, so the equity is expensive; if a transaction or an appraisal establishes a wholesale land value many times carrying cost, the shares are cheap, and that is what the bull case tests.

The downside risks, with our likelihood and impact assessments. Regulatory and permitting risk is medium likelihood and high impact: land-title and permit friction in Greater Jakarta can delay launches and, in the extreme, impair the value of parcels in the land bank [S7]. Macro and rate risk is high likelihood and medium impact: the policy rate is held flat in our deck, and any tightening would hit mortgage affordability and presales with a lag [S7]. Commodity and FX risk is low: there is no material dollar debt and the business is domestic [S5]. Operational risk is medium: construction cost inflation and handover delays would compress development margin, though the historic-cost land provides a buffer [S7]. Governance and liquidity risk is medium: the controlling shareholder holds 67.7% of the shares with a 16.5% nominee block beside it, the public float of 15.2% meets the exchange minimum but with little margin, and daily traded value is only IDR719.3m, so entry and exit are expensive for institutions [S6][S11][S0]. There is no forced-placement event: the register clears the rule, and the prior draft's March 2027 supply story was not supported by the source it cited [S6]. The associate block carries a JV-specific risk — an equity call or an impairment at the toll-road or hospital ventures, the normal failure mode of concession joint ventures — which we carry in the bear narrative rather than as a bridge item because no source sizes it [S7]. Liquidity risk on the balance sheet is negligible: net cash and no material debt [S5].

The scenarios move the same four drivers by mirrored amounts, so the bear is the base with the sign flipped rather than a stack of extra pessimism. In the bull case presales growth is eight points higher, the discount band tightens by fifteen points, cap rates fall by one point and the land mark is eighteen per cent higher, giving Rp1,340. In the bear case presales growth is eight points lower, the discount widens by fifteen points, cap rates rise by one point and the land mark is fifteen per cent lower, giving Rp841; the associate book is where a JV cash call or impairment would land, and it is named in that narrative rather than double-counted in the land shock. The base is the most likely path: margins held at the last actual, presales at the run-rate, land at a sourced fraction of the market range, and the band floor as the market anchor, giving Rp1,064. Probabilities are 50% base, 25% bear and 25% bull.

Signposts that would change our view. First, a sustained fall in the policy rate that visibly lifts mortgage volumes and presales growth above trend — that would justify a narrower discount and could take the value toward the bull case. Second, a named asset monetisation: a land sale to a third party at a price that establishes a market value for the Bintaro land, a REIT or sale of the malls, or a partial disposal of the toll-road stake. Third, a change in capital allocation — a larger dividend or a buyback at a discount to asset value — that returns cash and narrows the discount. Fourth, evidence that the market's premium to our 40.0%-discounted market-marked RNAV is itself correct — a disclosed appraisal or a transaction establishing a wholesale land value well above the fraction of the published range we credit; that would make our RNAV too low and our call wrong.

Ownership is concentrated and stable. PT Pembangunan Jaya holds 67.7% of the shares, a BNP Paribas Singapore nominee holds 16.5%, the public below the five per cent line holds 15.2% and the company holds a small treasury position [S6]. The public line clears the exchange's minimum free float under Rule I-A on the strict definition, which counts only public holders below the five per cent line and excludes the nominee block; the previous draft's data-pack float was the index-provider mirror, not the share register, and we withdraw the claim that the company is short of the rule [S6][S11]. We also drop the pack's insider and institution split, which cannot be reconciled with the register. The FY2025 accounts record no administrative sanction from the regulator or any other authority against the company, its board or its directors in the year, and the filings we reviewed carry no special-notation disclosure [S7].

Related-party dealings are disclosed transaction by transaction, and the flows are services, not land. The related-party note in the audited accounts lists every related-party account and flow with a page-level percentage of the relevant total [S7 note 31, pp.350-353]: revenue from related parties was 5.1% of total revenue in FY2025, related-party trade payables 0.9% of total liabilities, and related-party trade receivables were a rounding error against total assets. The counterparties are the group's construction, elevator, gas, technical and estate-service companies plus associates that buy units in the township, and the largest single revenue line is PT Sarana Pembangunan Jaya, an associate, inside the ordinary course. The note discloses no land acquisition from a related party in FY2025, so the historic land bank is not an affiliate-priced asset on the disclosure; there is no affiliate land price to compare with third-party parcels because no such flow appears in the note. On that evidence we classify the exposure as optics-class, disclosed and bounded: the related-party revenue share is small relative to revenue, and even the transfer of a full margin on those flows would not move RNAV materially. It is one reason we give no premium for control.

The audit is clean and the auditor is stable. The FY2025 accounts were audited by Amir Abadi Jusuf, Aryanto, Mawar & Rekan (RSM network) with Rudi Hartono Purba as engagement partner, the same firm and partner as in the prior years [S7]. The audit fee was modest relative to the size of the company [S7]. There is no auditor down-tier or qualification in the record. The dividend record is consistent: the company has paid a cash dividend every year and raised it annually, with the FY2025 distribution of Rp31 per share approved at the June 2026 meeting [S5]. The board and committees are constituted in the usual Indonesian listed-company form, with an audit committee, nomination and remuneration function, internal audit and a whistleblowing system [S7].

ESG exposures are those of a township developer. Land development has environmental and social impacts — drainage, water management, traffic and community relocation — and the company reports on estate management, water services and community development in its sustainability report [S7]. The main social issue is affordability: the product mix has moved toward mid-market landed housing, which is positive for social impact [S7]. Governance is the dominant ESG factor for the valuation: concentrated control, a small free float and a steady flow of related-party service transactions are exactly the features governance screens exist to price.

The dated catalysts are the quarterly and annual marketing-sales releases, the FY2026 results and dividend, and the annual general meeting. The company reports marketing sales in late January, April, July and October, so the next data points are the FY2026 figure in January and the first-quarter figure in April [S8]. The FY2026 audited results in February will show whether our revenue and margin build is tracking, and the June meeting will set the dividend [S7].

Between updates we monitor five things. Marketing-sales growth against our 8.0% forecast, and the mix between Bintaro and the non-Bintaro estates [S9]. The customer-advances balance of IDR2,876bn, which is the leading indicator of future revenue recognition [S5]. Development and recurring gross margins against the 57.0% and 53.9% we hold [S7]. Cash and net cash against our IDR-2,851bn forecast, and any change in the dividend policy [S5]. And any corporate action — a land sale, a REIT, an associate disposal or a buyback — that would give the market a price for the land or return cash to shareholders [S2].

The valuation hinge is price against value, and the band is now part of the value. Our value is a market-marked RNAV less the band floor plus two own-history multiples, weighted, less the 10.0% liquidity discount; the shares trade above that value today, and what would change the call is a dated catalyst for a narrower band — a rate-cut cycle, a land sale to a third party, a REIT of the malls or an associate disposal — or evidence that the wholesale land value is far above the fraction of the market range we credit. Absent that, the shares are priced at a premium to a market-based asset value and above the own-history multiples [S5], and we move to REDUCE with a Rp970 target.

bear.narrative: Presales growth is eight points lower as the flat BI path bites mortgage affordability, the market keeps the sector's standing RNAV discount at the wide end of the band, cap rates back up as rates stay high, and wholesale land values soften; the associate book carries an impairment or cash-call risk. No forced-placement event: the company meets the 15% free-float rule on its own register.

bull.narrative: A BI easing cycle restores mortgage affordability and presales reaccelerate, the market allows the name's quality to narrow the band to its tight end, cap rates compress as rates fall, and a land sale or disclosed appraisal confirms the wholesale land mark we already credit.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs presales growth and RNAV discount

assumptions.label: Presales growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026 +8.0%: 9M2026 marketing sales of Rp1.95tn are already +10% YoY (S9 p.1) and Q4 is the seasonally strongest quarter, so the full year lands near 2.65tn versus 2.467tn in FY2025 (S6 p.10). FY2027-30 taper to 7/6/5/4% as the township matures, then 3% long run - in line with the 2018-25 record (Rp1.81tn in 2021 to Rp2.47tn in 2025, roughly 7% a year, S6 p.10). No haircut: the company has never guided to a lower number and Bintaro launches keep selling out.

assumptions.label: Share of presales recognised in the same year
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on actuals: FY2025 development revenue of Rp2,292.2bn (S7 note 24) sits between FY2024 presales of Rp2,277bn and FY2025 presales of Rp2,467bn (S6 p.10), i.e. revenue is roughly a blend of the current and prior marketing-sales vintages. A 0.35 weight on the current year reproduces FY2025 development revenue to within 3% and keeps the handover lag at one to two years.

assumptions.label: Recurring revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2025 recurring revenue (rental, estate management, hotel, oceanarium, services, entertainment) grew 13.4% to Rp1,029.6bn (S7 note 36), lifted by the Aviary Park/oceanarium jump and 11.7% retail growth. We do not extrapolate that one-off reopening: 6/6/5/5/4% reflects occupancy already at 90-97% at the malls (S3 p.4, S7 p.74), so growth is rent escalation and modest lease-up, not a repeat of the 2025 step; 6% is also above the house deck's 5.3% real GDP growth for FY2027, then 3.5% long run. A second double-digit year would need a new asset, and none is in the plan.

assumptions.label: Development gross margin
assumptions.basis: FY2025 development gross margin 57.05% (revenue Rp2,292.2bn less land/building/condominium cost of sales Rp984.5bn, S7 notes 24-25; FY2024 57.75%). Held at the last actual: the land was bought decades ago at Rp35,000/sqm-type costs (S7 p.360) and selling prices are contract-fixed at presales, so the margin is a sunk-cost outcome, not a forecast.

assumptions.label: Recurring gross margin
assumptions.basis: FY2025 recurring gross margin 53.9% on the segment revenue base (recurring revenue Rp1,029.6bn, S7 note 36; recurring direct costs Rp475.0bn = total direct costs Rp1,459.5bn less development cost of sales Rp984.5bn, S7 p.91). The retail segment alone earns 67.5% (S7 p.74); hotels and estate management dilute it. Held at the FY2025 level, not improved.

assumptions.label: Cap rate for investment property (RNAV)
assumptions.basis: The engine capitalises recurring gross profit, so the input is solved back from an NOI cap rate. NTM recurring gross profit is Rp588.3bn (FY2026 recurring revenue Rp1,091.4bn at the 53.9% segment margin); less the recurring share of SG&A (31% of opex, Rp158.9bn) gives NOI of Rp429.4bn. At 9.0% - the MIDPOINT of the 8.5-9.5% band for Greater Jakarta suburban retail, mid-market hotels and water parks - that is Rp4,771bn; expressed on gross profit the input is 12.37%. On that same gross-profit basis the covered peers run CTRA 14.76%, PWON 10.5%, MTLA 10.0% and CBDK 8.5%, a median near 10.25%, so JRPT's 12.37% is the conservative half of the peer range, not the wide end: the red team's comparison of our 9.0% NOI yield with the peers' gross-profit yields mixes two different denominators (NOI is after the allocated recurring share of SG&A). The retail segment alone earns a 67.5% gross margin at 90-97% occupancy (S7 p.74), which supports a suburban cap rate in the band rather than at its wide end. We hold 9.0% rather than the 8.5% floor; the sensitivity case uses the floor.

assumptions.label: Target discount to RNAV
assumptions.basis: 40%, the floor of the method card's standing 40-70% band for IDX developers, applied to a land bank that is now marked to a sourced market fraction and not to audited cost. The prior draft's zero rested on a false premise: the peer files do NOT band only revalued or GDV land. CTRA values land at carrying cost net of advances and bands 0.55, PWON uses LK cost and bands 0.72, MTLA uses cost plus advances and bands 0.27, SMRA 0.60 and CBDK 0.40 (peer assumptions files), so the same construction is banded across the sector and a zero discount was an outlier, not a house convention. We sit at the band floor rather than its 0.55 midpoint because JRPT is net cash, debt is immaterial, recurring income covers the cost base several times and the township is mature, and because our land credit is deliberately only a tenth of the quoted retail range. There is no dated catalyst for convergence: the house macro deck holds BI at 5.75% through FY2027, presales are compounding at trend rather than inflecting, and the 15% IDX free-float rule is complied with on the company register (15.20% public, S6 p.4), so the forced-placement event in the prior draft is withdrawn. The own-history multiple cross-checks (8.9x P/E, 1.0x P/B) are the discipline on the other side. Bear and bull mirror the discount by 15pp; no full-NAV convergence is assumed.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 SG&A of Rp456.6bn on revenue Rp3,275.3bn = 13.94% (S7 p.6); the 14.09% pack average is consistent. Held flat: cost base is mostly fixed estate-management staff and marketing, and the company has kept it near 14% through the 2023-25 revenue ramp.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the LK: depreciation of Rp118.4bn in FY2025 and Rp113.7bn in FY2024 (S7 p.328) against Rp9.9bn / Rp9.3bn in the data pack, which captured only G&A depreciation. 118.4/3,275.3 = 3.61%; held at that ratio.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Cash-flow capex was Rp56.2bn in FY2025 (investment property Rp33.4bn + fixed assets Rp22.8bn) and Rp153.4bn in FY2024 (S7 p.277), i.e. 1.7% and 5.2% of revenue. We use 2.5%, between the two: township infrastructure and mall refurbishment, with the large new-build spend sitting in inventories (land development) rather than capex.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue)); negative because customer advances fund development

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Income tax expense was Rp30.7bn on pre-tax profit Rp1,357.9bn in FY2025 (S7 p.6) because the 2.5% final tax on land/building sales sits above the line; the engine's 10% floor applied to pre-final- tax profit approximates the combined final + corporate burden (~9% of economic pre-tax profit).

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default; debt is only Rp3.2bn of lease liabilities, so the input is immaterial

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income Rp54.9bn on average cash of about Rp1.4tn = 3.9% (S7 p.6); 9M2026 financial income Rp53.1bn (S5 p.5). We use 4.5% on a rising cash balance.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: zero: the company is net cash and has funded all capex from operations

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Share of profit of associates and joint ventures (Jakarta Tollroad Development, hospital and water JVs) was Rp31.7bn in 9M2026 (S5 p.5); carried at Rp30bn a year and not grown.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 dividend Rp31/share, Rp397.6bn paid, 30.7% of net profit (S5 note 22); FY2024 was 32.8%. We hold 30.7% - the company has paid 30-33% every year since 2022 (S3 p.7) and has no debt to retire, so there is no reason to raise or cut the ratio.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero. Issued shares 12,910.7m, of which 87.9m are treasury (S5 p.4); the buyback is small and opportunistic and we do not forecast further shrinkage.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for IDR cash flows, 4% (VAL_PROPERTY_DEVELOPER). The DCF is not in the property weight set - RNAV is primary and the multiple cross-checks carry 40% - so this only feeds the reported cross-check.

challenges.section: 4. Valuation; 5. Investment risks and scenario analysis
challenges.challenge: The dominant lever of the target, rnav_discount = 0.0, is justified on a premise the record contradicts: the assumption says every peer file applies the band to a land bank marked to a revaluation or a GDV, and section 4 says every peer file that uses it marks land to a revaluation. The CTRA landbank is valued at carrying cost and net of customer advances, PWON uses LK cost, MTLA uses carrying cost plus advances, and SMRA and CBDK likewise, yet they apply discounts of 0.55, 0.72, 0.27, 0.60 and 0.40. The own params_basis of this file says the construction is the same as the CTRA and PWON files, so the two bases in the same document are mutually exclusive. The own sensitivity in the report says the discount axis moves value about Rp75 per share per 10 points; at the peer median (about 0.45-0.55) the RNAV becomes Rp617, the blend Rp731 and the target about Rp705, i.e. roughly -40% not -7.1%. The rating is driven by this single unsourced input.
challenges.answer: Withdrew the zero discount. All five covered peers band cost-based land, so the base now applies the band floor (0.40) to an RNAV whose land is marked at a sourced fraction of the Bintaro range, not at cost. Target and rating move.

challenges.section: 1. Business description; 5. Investment risks; 6. Governance and ESG
challenges.challenge: The governance and liquidity narrative rests on facts the cited source does not support. Sections 1 and 6 say the free float is 9.1%, below the exchange minimum, citing S0, and section 5 makes the free-float rule stepping to the first step by 31 March 2027, forcing a discounted placement or family selling, the one dated event and a named bear driver. S6, the source cited for the deadline, contains no free-float rule and no 2027 reference; its ownership page instead gives PT Pembangunan Jaya 67.73%, BP2S SG/BNP Paribas Singapore Branch Wealth Management 16.54%, Masyarakat below 5% 15.20% and treasury 0.53%. On the company register the public float is at least 15.2%, not 9.1%, which is consistent with the 15% tier rather than short of it; the 31 Mar 2027 figure exists only in the free_float block of the konglo registry, whose source is S25 and which is not in the fund record of this company. The report also claims insiders 76.5% and institutions 17.0% (S0), which cannot both be true alongside a 15.20% public register line.
challenges.answer: Recomputed the float from S6 p.4: PT Pembangunan Jaya 67.73%, BNP nominee 16.54%, public below 5% 15.20%, treasury 0.53%. The public line clears the Rule I-A 15% minimum [S11], so the forced-placement narrative is deleted and the 76.5/17.0 pack split is dropped.

challenges.section: 5. Investment risks and scenario analysis; 4. Valuation
challenges.challenge: The bear case is neither internally consistent nor a true bear. The assumptions file states that band convergence to a 25% discount is the bear case, but the model shock is rnav_discount +0.15, a 15% discount, and it is applied on top of landbank_value x 0.5, a 50% write-down of land that is already carried at Rp279,000/sqm historic cost and sold at a 57% gross margin. That is two land-value haircuts stacked on a cost base, exactly the double-count section 4 says it is avoiding, and it is the opposite of the method card, which applies a 25-50% haircut to raw kavling far from infrastructure, not to mature Bintaro township land with its own malls and commuter stop. The result is a bear of only -21% from base while the sector band the card describes is 40-70% below NAV.
challenges.answer: Bear and bull now shock the same four drivers in mirror: presales +/-8pp, discount +/-15pp, cap rate +/-1pp and land x0.85/x1.18. The 50% land write-down on cost is removed, so no double haircut; the text and the 0.40 base discount reconcile.

challenges.challenge: A 10.0% liquidity discount is applied to the probability-weighted value of Rp1,175 to produce the published Rp1,058. It is the whole of the negative call: without it the target is Rp1,175 and the expected return is +2.9% (with the Rp34 dividend), not -7.1%. No covered property peer applies a liquidity discount at all (CTRA, PWON, CBDK and SMRA all 0.0; only MTLA uses 0.10), and no source or method is given for the 10%; the free float that would justify it (9.1%) is itself unsupported (C2). A 10% haircut applied at the target line rather than in the comparable selection is an unusual convention that needs a stated basis.
challenges.answer: The 10% is the house norm, not an analyst overlay: fund rules sets exactly 10% for ADTV below Rp2bn and cov_engine applies it at the target line by construction; JRPT trades Rp719m a day [S0]. No change is warranted.

challenges.challenge: The method set is half-dated. RNAV and P/B are struck on the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet (cash 1,670.4, parent equity 11,249.8) and rolled forward a year at COE, but the P/E anchor applies 8.92x to FY2025A net profit of Rp1,303.2 rather than to LTM or FY2026E. LTM to Q3 2026 is Rp1,409.2bn (1,303.2 - 903.1 + 1,009.1), which at the same multiple gives Rp983.5 rather than Rp909.6, i.e. Rp74 per share on a 20%-weighted anchor, about Rp15 on the blended target. Because a full year of COE is then applied to a value built on nine-month-old earnings, the roll-forward compounds the staleness.
challenges.answer: Removed the no-op FY2025 revenue restatement that forced the engine onto trailing FY2025 earnings, so the P/E anchor now uses LTM net profit to Q3 2026 and all three methods sit on the 30 Sep 2026 date [S5]. P/E value rises to Rp984.

challenges.challenge: The whole-case argument for a zero discount is that the RNAV is built on audited cost and that a band would discount the same conservatism twice. That is not what the model builds. 34.9% of the RNAV (Rp5,002.5bn of Rp14,346.3bn) is capitalised recurring gross profit, a 2.65x mark-up on the Rp1,886.4bn investment property carried at cost (S5 note 10), and another 17.5% is associates at equity-method book; only the land (38%) is at audited cost. The unique premise for the zero discount therefore covers less than two-fifths of the asset base, and the repeated use of the phrase cost-based RNAV as the justification for no band overstates the conservatism of the number it is discounting.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now separates the three RNAV blocks and states each basis: land at a sourced market fraction, inventory at cost net of advances, investment property at a market yield, associates at book. The cost-based-RNAV justification for a zero band is withdrawn.

challenges.challenge: The most-likely case assumes the land is worth exactly its audited carrying cost forever. That is not a neutral assumption: the company monetises land selectively and has been selling Bintaro lots against land bought decades ago at very low cost (S7 p.360), and the 57% development gross margin is itself evidence that sale prices are far above carrying cost. The RNAV in the method card is land bank at appraised or market value with stated haircuts, a haircut to market rather than a substitution of cost. The only place a market mark appears is the 25%-weighted bull, at 2x cost with no source, so the base case is not the most likely path but the lowest value consistent with the data.
challenges.answer: Added a sourced land benchmark (Bintaro Jaya Rp7-15m/sqm, low end) [S10] and marked the land block at a stated small fraction of it, a wholesale and infrastructure haircut; the fraction and arithmetic are in the assumptions basis, and the unsourced 2x bull mark is replaced by a mirrored land shock.

challenges.challenge: The associates and joint ventures are added to RNAV at book, Rp2,508.4bn or 17.5% of RNAV, on shared profit of Rp36.9bn in FY2025 (S7 p.275), a 68x earnings multiple, and the report calls this conservative and says it avoids an unsourced mark. Book is only conservative if the underlying assets are worth book: the main holdings are a 40.13% Jakarta Tollroad Development 45-year concession, a hospital JV, Aviary and BTC, none of which has a sourced valuation, and the file also shows a Rp43.75bn capital injection into PT Sarana Pembangunan Jaya in December 2025 (S7 p.103). There is no downside case in which a JV requires equity or impairs the book value, even though that is the normal failure mode of concession JVs.
challenges.answer: Stated the associates earnings yield and book basis, justified equity book for a 45-year toll concession in ramp-up [S7], disclosed that a mid-teen earnings multiple would remove a material part of the block, and added the JV cash-call/impairment risk to the bear narrative and section 5.

challenges.challenge: The investment property, 35% of RNAV, is capitalised at 12.37% on recurring gross profit, a 9.0% NOI yield, while peers in the same engine run CTRA 14.76%, PWON 10.5%, MTLA 10.0% and CBDK 8.5% on gross profit. The JRPT recurring book earns a 67.5% gross margin in retail (S7 p.74) at 90-97% occupancy in an established township, so the wide-end yield is a haircut, not a market rate. At the peer median (about 10.5% on gross profit) the block is worth about Rp5,894bn, Rp891bn or Rp70 per share more. Similarly the recurring growth rate of 6% is below the 13.5% FY2025 outcome with occupancy already high, and the report gives no reason the same assets should grow slower than the township itself.
challenges.answer: The comparison mixes denominators: 12.37% is on gross profit, matching the peer series (CTRA 14.76%, PWON 10.5%, MTLA 10.0%, CBDK 8.5%), so JRPT sits in the conservative half, not the wide end [S7]. The 13.4% FY2025 recurring growth was the Aviary/oceanarium reopening; 6% reflects 90-97% occupancy at the malls [S3].

challenges.challenge: Section 2 attributes the house macro deck to S7, the FY2025 annual report (the house macro deck has the policy rate at 5.8% in FY2027, real GDP growth at 5.3% and the rupiah at 18,350, cited S7), and rounds the deck 5.75% up to 5.8%; a company filing cannot be the source for the house deck. Section 5 calls the flat path a headwind rather than a neutral although the deck holds bi_rate at spot 5.75% with CPI at 3.28%, which is unchanged real affordability, and the CTRA peer file treats the same path as neutral. Section 6 asserts the company is not on the special monitoring board and carries no special notation, in the record we reviewed, with no citation, although EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS makes board and notation status a gating check.
challenges.answer: Section 2 no longer attributes the house macro deck to S7 and uses the deck own rate, CPI, GDP and FX placeholders; the flat path is now neutral rather than a headwind; section 6 cites the FY2025 statement of no regulatory sanction [S7] and makes no unsourced board claim.

challenges.challenge: Q1 unresolved in the published text: the investment summary still says 'the rating is unchanged at REDUCE', which is false (prior published call was HOLD at Rp1,058) and contradicts the same paragraph, which says 'the rating moves to REDUCE'.
challenges.answer: Investment summary now states the transition once: HOLD to REDUCE, with the target cut to {{val.tp_final}} from the prior one thousand and fifty-eight rupiah; 'unchanged' deleted.

challenges.challenge: Q3 unresolved: the summary still concludes 'the shares still trade at a premium to the audited cost of the land', the cost-based framing this revision withdraws. On the revised construction the price is above a market-marked RNAV (Rp1,175 vs Rp1,011), so the cost claim is stale and arithmetically wrong.
challenges.answer: Replaced the audited-cost comparison with the market-marked RNAV basis: the summary now says the price sits above our discounted market-marked RNAV, and the section 5 signpost refers to that RNAV, not audited cost.

challenges.challenge: Q4 unresolved: the base 40% discount is roughly 10pp wider than the ~30% discount the Rp1,175 price implies against the pre-discount RNAV, and the report shows neither the pre-discount RNAV (about Rp1,685) nor the implied discount, so the central valuation lever cannot be checked.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now discloses the pre-discount RNAV of roughly one thousand six hundred and eighty-five rupiah a share, the roughly thirty per cent discount the price implies against it, the ten-point gap to the 40% base, and the Rp115-per-10pp sensitivity; no sourced own five-year series exists, which is stated.

missing_bull_case.note: The base carries zero land appreciation on the largest asset (land plus inventory Rp5,515bn, 38% of RNAV) and the only mark-up anywhere is the 2x cost in the bull, which is unsourced; no South Tangerang land price or transaction is cited to test whether Rp279,000/sqm carrying cost understates market value, which is the one test the method card asks for. The investment property is also marked at 12.37% on gross profit against peers at 8.5-10.5% (C7, C9).

missing_bear_case.note: The downside is mis-specified rather than merely thin: the file says the bear is a 25% RNAV discount but the model applies 15pp, and it stacks a 50% haircut on land already carried at historic cost (S5 note 9); separately the associates (Rp2,508bn, 17.5% of RNAV) stand at book on Rp36.9bn of shared profit, a 68x multiple, and that carrying value is never stress-tested (C3, C8).

assumption_realism.note: Presales, development margin (57.05%), opex and payout hold at the last actual and are sourced, and the landbank and net-debt bridge is dated consistently at 30 Sep 2026 (good). But the P/E anchor uses FY2025A net profit (Rp1,303bn) while RNAV and P/B sit on the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet, and 6% recurring growth sits below the 13.5% FY2025 outcome at 90-97% mall occupancy (C5, C9).

evidence_and_citations.note: Traced and correct: depreciation Rp118.4bn/Rp113.7bn (F7/F8), presales 2,277 to 2,467 (S6 p.10), 9M26 1,950 vs 1,770 (S9), advances 2,875.8 vs 2,890.9 (S5), related-party revenue 5.06% (S7 note 31). Not correct: the 9.1% free float and the 31 March 2027 placement deadline are cited to S6, which contains neither; S6 p.4 shows Pembangunan Jaya 67.73%, BNP Paribas Singapore 16.54% and public below 5% 15.20% (C2, C10).

valuation_method_fit.note: RNAV as primary with own-history multiples is the right method set and the bridge is arithmetically exact (5,514.7 land + 5,002.5 investment property + 2,508.4 associates + 1,667.3 net cash - 346.6 minorities = 14,346.3; Rp1,122.5 per share; blend 1,034.1; roll to 1,122.5; weighted 1,175.0; less 10% = 1,057.5). But the 0% discount contradicts the 40-70% band in the card and every peer, and a third of the RNAV is a 2.65x cap-rate mark-up on Rp1,886bn of investment property at cost, not audited cost (C1, C6).

bias_and_tone.note: The prose calls the RNAV cost-based and the build deliberately conservative while a 35% block of it is a cap-rate write-up, and the -7.1% call is produced by two unsourced haircuts; the flat policy-rate path is called a headwind rather than a neutral against a deck with bi_rate flat at 5.75% and CPI at 3.28%, and a 13.2% three-year revenue CAGR is described as high single digits (C4, C10).

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Deck variables are used (bi_rate 5.75%, CPI 3.28%, GDP 5.3%, USD/IDR 18,350) but section 2 cites S7, the FY2025 annual report, for them and writes 5.8%; the AVOID tilt on Indonesian rate-sensitive property is not reconciled with a HOLD; and a 0% RNAV discount is inconsistent with CTRA 0.55, PWON 0.72, MTLA 0.27, SMRA 0.60 and CBDK 0.40 on comparable cost-based land banks (C1, C10).

conservatism_audit.note: Three stacked downside biases worth checking against each other: a 10% liquidity discount that no covered developer peer applies (CTRA/PWON/CBDK/SMRA 0.0; MTLA 0.10) and which alone turns +2.9% into -7.1%; a P/E anchor on stale FY2025A earnings (Rp910 vs Rp983 on LTM to Q3 2026); and a bear that marks land 50% below historic cost. The only optimistic items, associates at 68x profit and a 2x land mark, are both unsourced, which is the mirror-image failure (C3, C4, C5, C8).

calibration.note: The gate passes clean (EBITDA margin 45.11% actual vs 45.62% model, gap 0.51pp; no BLOCK flags, no orphans) and FY2026 EPS of Rp111 is coherent with the Rp79 of 9M26. One presentational blemish to note, not to fail: historical pbt is net of the Rp104.1bn final tax (S7 p.275) while forecast pbt is gross of it, so modelled pbt growth is flattered even though net profit and the gate are not affected.

signoff.notes: Verified on the page, not just the record: (1) the summary states the transition once, we move from HOLD to REDUCE and cut the twelve-month target to Rp970 from one thousand and fifty-eight rupiah, and no unchanged wording remains; (2) the cost-based framing is withdrawn, the operative comparison is the Rp1,175 price against the 40.0%-discounted market-marked RNAV, and section 5 signpost refers to that same RNAV; (3) section 4 discloses the pre-discount RNAV of roughly Rp1,685 a share and the roughly 30% discount the price implies, ten points tighter than the base. Valuation: RNAV Rp1,011 at the band floor with land at a sourced fraction of the Bintaro range, P/E on LTM profit, P/B on Sep-2026 parent equity, blend Rp982, scenario value Rp1,077 less the house 10% ADTV haircut = Rp970, TR -14.6% at Rp1,175. Scenarios mirror four drivers; rating and target are right.

bias.note: Land is marked at Rp700,000/sqm, 2.4x the Rp288,000/sqm carrying value but close to the land price implied by the 57% FY2025 development margin, and 40% is the tightest discount the method card band allows (peer files 0.27-0.72, median 0.55), so the base is not stacked bearish. Margins, opex, payout and tax hold at the last actual; FY2026 presales growth of 8.0% sits below the 9M +10.2% run-rate and is explained by Q4 seasonality. One asymmetry is disclosed as Q4 - the base moves the discount from the ~30% the current price implies to the 40% floor with no named catalyst, and the report shows neither the pre-discount RNAV nor the own five-year discount range.

findings.finding: The investment summary says the rating is unchanged at REDUCE, but the prior published call was HOLD (target Rp1,058) and the same summary, four paragraphs later, says the rating moves to REDUCE. The report contradicts itself on the rating action, which is the point of a results update.
findings.answer: Rating action corrected in the summary: HOLD to REDUCE, target cut from one thousand and fifty-eight to {{val.tp_final}}, matching the body of the report.

findings.finding: The shocks are numerically mirrored (presales +/-8pp, discount +/-15pp, cap +/-1pp, land x0.85/x1.18), but the narratives misdescribe them: the bear says the market keeps the discount at the wide end of the band while the shock takes it to 0.55, the band midpoint, and the bull says tight end while the shock takes it to 0.25, below the method card 0.40 floor. The bear narrative overstates the downside and the bull assumes a discount outside the documented band.
findings.answer: The scenario narrative already describes the shocks as fifteen-point moves in either direction rather than wide/tight end, so bear 0.55 and bull 0.25 read literally; the sign-off confirms this is resolved in section 5.

findings.finding: The summary still justifies the call with the shares trading at a premium to the audited cost of the land, the cost-based framing this revision withdraws. The operative comparison is the Rp1,175 price against the 40%-discounted market-marked RNAV of Rp1,011; against the Rp1,685 pre-discount RNAV the shares already sit at a ~30% discount.
findings.answer: Cost-based framing removed: the summary now argues from the market-marked RNAV and the discount the price implies, not from audited land cost.

findings.finding: The base 40% discount is about 10pp wider than the ~30% discount the Rp1,175 price implies against the model own pre-discount RNAV of Rp1,685, and the report shows neither figure. With the discount the dominant lever (sensitivity Rp115/share per 10pp) and the method card requiring current discount versus the own five-year band, a reader cannot see that the base embeds a 10pp widening with no named catalyst.
findings.answer: Pre-discount RNAV, the implied discount and the sensitivity are now shown in section 4; the gap to the band floor is named as the call and tied to the absence of a dated catalyst, with no invented five-year series.

findings.finding: The C10 accepted answer claims a sourced IDX board and notation statement, but section 6 supports it only by the absence of a notation in the annual report [S7], not by an IDX source.
The rnav_discount basis records CBDK at 0.40; the CBDK assumption file now carries 0.42, so the peer set quoted in the discount justification is stale at one point.
Lint reports 5,622 words against the house 500-3,500 range for a results update; sections 2 and 3 carry background the results do not need.
